title: He was in the bloodline of Jesus…
paragraphs: He was in the bloodline of Jesus…

Not a king.
Not a prophet.
Not a miracle worker.
Because some of us are living like Hezron—hidden, quiet, unseen—and we’ve started to believe a lie:
“If no one notices me… maybe God doesn’t either.”
Because the Bible is about to expose something deeper.
And sometimes it gets darker than that.
You look at your past—mistakes, shame, things you wish you could erase—and you start to believe your life is just… background noise.
What if you’re not just overlooked…
Hezron appears in a genealogy—those long lists we usually skip.

Genesis 46:12 —
“The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah… and the sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.”

Ruth 4:18 —
“Now this is the genealogy of Perez: Perez fathered Hezron…”

Matthew 1:3 —
“Judah the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar, and Perez the father of Hezron…”
Hezron is not just a name.
A quiet, almost invisible bridge between scandal and salvation.
Judah—his ancestor—was involved in sin and moral failure (Genesis 38).
Tamar’s story was filled with pain, injustice, and desperation.
This was not a clean lineage.
Some scholars interpret genealogies as more than historical records—they are theological declarations. They show us that God is not intimidated by human failure; He weaves redemption through it.
Hezron’s significance is not in what he did.
It’s in where God placed him.
Right in the middle of a redemption story he didn’t control.
Because the Gospel does not begin with perfect people.

Romans 3:23 —
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
Sin is not just what we do.
It’s what we are apart from God.
Instead of abandoning the line, He enters it.
Because Jesus did not come from a flawless story.
He came INTO a flawed story.
To redeem it from the inside out.
No amount of effort, religion, or performance could clean the stain.
But Jesus Christ—the Son of God—stepped into human history.
Lived the life we failed to live.
Died the death we deserved on the cross.

Ephesians 1:7 —
“In Him we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of His grace.”
Hezron’s quiet name sits in a loud truth:
And if God can use a lineage marked by sin to bring forth the Savior…
What makes you think your story is beyond redemption?
They are not the end of your story.
They are the very place where grace can begin.

Acts 3:19 —
“Repent therefore, and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out.”
Because the same God who saw Hezron in a long list of names…
Sees you in a world of billions.
And He is not asking you to be famous.
He is asking you to be His.
Will you keep living like your life doesn’t matter?
Or will you surrender and let God write you into His redemption story?
Type “OPEN MY HEART” if you’re ready to stop hiding and start surrendering.
